hook.text: In 2021, a container from Shanghai to Los Angeles cost $20,000. In 2019, it cost $2,000. Same box, 10x the price.

buildup.text: COVID shut ports, grounded planes, and idled factories. The global supply chain shattered simultaneously.

discovery.text: Just-in-time manufacturing meant no buffers. One factory closing in Taiwan could halt car production in Detroit.

twist.text: Chip shortages from a single region made new cars scarce. Used car prices jumped 40% in one year.

climax.text: Globalization made everything cheaper for decades. It also made everything fragile and interconnected.

quiz.question: Why did supply chain disruptions cause inflation in 2021?
options: Shortages made goods scarce, driving prices up
